title.narrative: Response Preparedness Project South Sudan (2022-2025)

description.narrative: South Sudan Red Cross & local communities

The Response Preparedness (RP) project in South Sudan aims to strengthen localized response capacity of South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) and local community structures to address the enormous and unprecedented level of humanitarian needs increasing over the years due increased frequency and intensity of climate related hazards.
The SSRC branches of and local communities in Pibor and Kapoeta

The combined effects of flooding, food insecurity, cholera, malaria, and COVID-19 coupled with very low levels of development and high levels of poverty among the population, will continue to expose communities to the adverse effects of disaster and shocks, calling for a concerted effort to strengthen local capacity to prepare for, anticipate, and respond to disasters and protect lives in disaster prone areas of the country.

The project will apply a multi-hazard approach to ensure a more effective and efficient humanitarian system throughout the full disaster continuum. It will strengthen SSRC capacity according to identified needs and improvements from the PER assessment conducted in 2019. In addition, it seeks to strengthen SSRC capacity in anticipatory action and forecast based financing through developing a simplified Early Warning System. NLRC and SSRC will be supported in this project by the Red Cross Climate Centre and the 510 data & digital team.
